quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When you are driving through an intersection.
When you are passing a bicycle.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When you are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails are ahead and to the right.
A hotel is ahead and to the right.
A hospital is ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hospital is ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the lane ahead is clear.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.
A driver must stop, then proceed when the way is clear.
A driver must stop, then proceed when a green light or green arrow appears.
A driver may turn in the direction the red arrow is pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver must stop, then proceed when a green light or green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow on a traffic light means you must come to a complete stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines divide lanes moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mark lane dividers and road edges. Broken white lines divide lanes and can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you a false sense of confidence.
It hurts your ability to think clearly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, coordination, and balance. It also hurts your vision and your ability to judge distance, making it hard to react to what happens around you.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Drivers under 18 cannot text or talk on a cell phone while driving.
Drivers 18 and older must use a hands-free device when talking on a cell phone while driving.
Drivers 18 and older cannot text while driving.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 cannot talk or text on a cell phone while driving. Drivers 18 and older must use a hands-free device if they use a cell phone while driving.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Drive carefully and slow down.
Do not use high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, slow down and drive carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead because they light up the road better in fog.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate with each other.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas behind them that cannot be seen in side mirrors or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before proceeding.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see down all tracks clearly. Even with one track, check again for another train approaching before you cross.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic go before you enter the intersection or roadway.

questions.question: Which of the following does not happen when you drink alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes slow down.
Your ability to judge speed and distance gets worse.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, makes it harder to judge speed and distance, reduces your recovery from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: U-turns are not allowed.
U-turns are allowed.
Winding road ahead.
Sharp left turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it is a prohibition sign. Where this sign is posted, U-turns are not permitted.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is a passing lane and the vehicle ahead is turning left or waiting to turn left. You may also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist does not obey traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always receive a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as drivers. Both bicyclists and drivers who break traffic laws can be ticketed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. Where this sign is posted, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You are waiting at a stop sign behind other vehicles. After they pass through with no cross traffic, what should you do?

options.text: You can go through without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
You can slowly roll past the stop sign.
You can follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Don't skip the stop just because other cars went through.

questions.question: When can you proceed through a stop sign that has no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before entering the intersection at a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before the intersection and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run into the street without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run into the street without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful in areas with children. Children may not understand danger and may suddenly run into the street without looking.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Stop completely when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: When two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign intersection, what should happen?

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to indicate that they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: When must you yield to a stopped transit bus that is about to re-enter traffic?

options.text: Only if there are cars behind you.
If the bus has turned on its hazard lights.
When the bus has its turn signal and flashing "Yield" sign activated.
Never. The bus must wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the bus has its turn signal and flashing "Yield" sign activated.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a stopped transit bus when it signals with its turn signal and has a flashing "Yield" sign on the back. Slow down or move over to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to stop at a railroad crossing. Not all crossings have gates or flashing lights. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: What colors are warning signs that show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs showing upcoming hazards are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
There is construction work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is construction work ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs indicate construction, maintenance, or emergency work. They have black letters or symbols.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary.
Try to get in front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the chance of a collision. If you drive faster than traffic around you, you will have to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, within the legal speed limit, and pass only when needed.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering a crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the stop line and before any crosswalk.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: Why must you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: The person is deaf.
The person is a police officer.
The person is blind.
The person has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The person is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and yield the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road. This includes the back seat and truck beds. You also cannot keep an open container of alcohol where a driver or passenger normally sits.

questions.question: How does the type of alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can hurt your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Drive straight. It is the bicyclist's job to move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to tell the bicyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on normal roads, or 5 feet on higher speed roads or when there are multiple bicyclists. Do not honk unless needed, as it can startle them and cause a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when you see other drivers acting angry?

options.text: Do not make eye contact.
Do not use hand gestures.
Get away from the situation.
Do all of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of these.
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, keep your distance from them. Avoid eye contact and do not make gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever is safe to stay away from danger.
